version_code.selector_function: sig_test (R/descr.R lines 2306-3001); defaults in descr() lines 263-275; per-variable override precedence in descr_var lines 849-857

code_preprocessing.rule: descr() converts Date/POSIXt to factor, difftime to numeric, and every other non-numeric column (character, logical, factor) with forcats::as_factor() + fct_explicit_na(); ordered factors stay ordered. 'Categorical' in the diagram therefore means 'factor after this coercion'.
code_preprocessing.consequence: Numeric storage (e.g. 0/1 or 1-5 codes) always enters the Numerical branch; character columns always enter Nominal with level order by first appearance.

code_preprocessing.rule: group column coerced with as_factor(); rows with NA group dropped unless format_options$omit_missings_in_group = FALSE.

Inside sig_test: drop NA var, the '(Missing)' var level (unless include_categorical_missings_in_test) and the '(Missing)' group (unless include_group_missings_in_test); droplevels(); n_levels_group = remaining group levels (1 when group is NULL); n_levels_var = remaining var levels.
'No test' when the factor has 1 level, or a numeric var has <= 1 nonmissing observation in some group, or only 1 observation overall.
Evaluation order: (1) is.ordered(var) || (is.numeric(var) && nonparametric) -> Ordinal; (2) is.numeric(var) -> Continuous; (3) is.factor(var) -> Nominal.
If test_override (global test_options or var_options[[v]]) is set, the tree is skipped entirely; per-variable settings take precedence over global ones.

Paired tests need test_options$indices (vector or a column name). guess_id defaults to FALSE in code (the descr() documentation text says TRUE is the default). Without indices, paired branches call stop(), which descr_var converts into 'Test errored, check console output.'

nodes.source_label: Which test is chosen for the variable var?

Variable is a factor (after descr() coercion of character/logical/Date columns).
Variable is stored as numeric (integer or double).
Unordered factor.
Ordered factor, or numeric variable with nonparametric = TRUE; analysed with rank tests.
Numeric variable with nonparametric = FALSE; analysed with t/ANOVA-type tests. The code does not check continuity or normality.
Nominal variable with exact = FALSE: large-sample tests.
Nominal variable with exact = TRUE: exact or unconditional exact tests.

Asymptotic nominal test for independent groups or one sample.
Exact nominal test for matched observations (requires subject IDs).
Exact nominal test for independent groups or one sample.
Rank test for repeated measurements on the same subjects.
Rank test for independent groups or one sample.
Parametric test for repeated measurements on the same subjects.
Parametric test for independent groups or one sample.
Two occasions (group levels) x binary response, matched by subject ID.

ci_call.note: A different unconditional exact procedure from the reported p-value; in run R2 its p-value happened to equal the boschloo() p (0.0480581).

boschloo_dispatch.descrtab2_own_validation: c_other_software_comparison.Rmd (in the 2.1.16 tarball and GitHub head) states DescrTab2 uses tsmethod = central and that no comparison is readily available for this option; it compares tsmethod = minlike with Exact::exact.test instead.
observations_for_09A: Single table 7/20 vs 2/22 (2026-10-03, provisional, not validation): exact2x2 central p 0.048058109 with default nPgrid = 100 vs 0.048058311 with nPgrid = 2000; Exact::exact.test(tsmethod = 'central') 0.048058312. minlike: exact2x2 0.045135313 (default) vs 0.045138295 (nPgrid 2000); Exact 'square' 0.045138318. The default grid gave slightly smaller p-values on this table.

Exact::exact.test tsmethod 'square' corresponds to exact2x2 boschloo tsmethod 'minlike' (exact2x2 calls uncondExact2x2 with tsmethod = 'square' internally); this is a naming correspondence from code reading, to be confirmed in 09A.

gaps.text: 'Continuous and normally distributed' is never checked; the route depends only on numeric storage and the nonparametric flag.
Exact '1xL table' -> exact binomial: code supports only L = 2 (p0 = 0.5); L >= 3 gives 'No test'.
Paired nominal with >= 3 categories gives 'No test' (no Stuart-Maxwell/Bowker); exact paired designs other than 2x2 give 'No test'.
var_equal = TRUE route (Student two-sample t) and override-only tests (Cochran-Armitage, Jonckheere-Terpstra) are not in the diagram.
'large n' is nonmissing n > boschloo_max_n (default 200, NULL disables); not stated in the diagram.

6 of 18 diagram leaf labels are not valid test_override strings: 'Cochrane's Q test'; 'Pearson's Chi-squared test'; 'Wilcoxon's two-sample signed-rank test'; 'Friedman's test'; 'Mixed model ANOVA, subject ID as random effect'; 'Welch's t-test'. print_test_names() also lists the misspelt 'Exact binomal test', which returns p = NA (run O4).
Ordinal '1 group' only when no group is supplied; a supplied single-level group gives 'No test'. Continuous paired else-branch sends a 1-group case to Mixed model ANOVA (code reading only).
Paired branches need subject IDs (indices); guess_id defaults to FALSE in code although the descr() help says TRUE.
Missing-value options (include_categorical_missings_in_test, include_group_missings_in_test) change the table dimension and therefore the test (Boschloo -> Fisher; runs M2, M3).
Pre-tree coercion and skip rules (character/logical/Date -> nominal; numeric codes -> numerical; single-level factors and <= 1 observation per group -> 'No test') are not shown.
Confidence-interval methods and two-sided conventions per test are not in the diagram (Boschloo central vs Fisher stats definition; McNemar CI unpaired).

DescrTab2 is archived on CRAN (2025-10-18); 2.1.26 exists only on GitHub. Selector logic identical in 2.1.16 and 2.1.26 head; print_CI default differs. inferguidR cannot rely on a CRAN-installable DescrTab2.
Per METHOD_TREE_SOURCES, numeric type semantics (when numeric storage means categories or ordinal scores) must be confirmed by the user; this audit only documents DescrTab2's storage-type behaviour.

Not run in this audit: Wilcoxon paired, Kruskal-Wallis, chi-squared goodness-of-fit, Cochran-Armitage, Jonckheere-Terpstra, Fisher workspace limits on large r x c tables, the continuous paired 1-group path, boschloo_max_n = NULL at n > 200.

Numerical correctness of exact2x2::boschloo (central) and of the nuisance-grid accuracy was not validated here; DescrTab2-vs-exact2x2 equality (run R2) is an integration check only. Belongs to 09A/11.

checks_run.environment: R 4.6.1, DescrTab2 2.1.16, exact2x2 1.7.0, DescTools 0.99.60, nlme 3.1.170, forcats 1.0.1, Exact 3.3
checks_run.note: Scenario scripts were run from a temporary scratch directory and deleted afterwards; inputs and outputs are summarised here and in descrtab2-audit.md. These are dispatch/integration checks, not numerical validation.

scenarios.R1: unordered binary 2x2, defaults -> Pearson's chi-squared test, p 0.0409796, chi-squared approximation warnings
scenarios.R2: same data, exact = TRUE, n = 42 -> Boschloo's test, p 0.0480581 = direct exact2x2::boschloo(7, 20, 2, 22); CI -0.5680218 to -0.0021725 = uncondExact2x2 FisherAdj difference
scenarios.R3: var_options test_override Boschloo with exact = FALSE -> Boschloo's test, same p
scenarios.R4: exact = TRUE, additional_test_args tsmethod = 'minlike' -> 'Test errored' (match.arg in uncondExact2x2); direct minlike p 0.0451353
scenarios.R5: exact = TRUE, additional_test_args alternative = 'less' -> p 0.0240291 = direct boschloo less
scenarios.R6: exact = TRUE, n = 201 -> Fisher's exact test with warning, p 0.048385 = stats::fisher.test
scenarios.R8: ordered binary factor, exact = TRUE -> Mann-Whitney's U test, HL CI 0 to 0
scenarios.R9: numeric 0/1, exact = TRUE -> Welch's two-sample t-test
scenarios.R10: character variable, rows reordered -> Boschloo's test; levels by first appearance (var: no, yes; group: B, A)
scenarios.R11: supplied group with one level, exact = TRUE -> Exact binomial test
scenarios.R12: no group, exact = TRUE -> Exact binomial test, p equals binom.test(9, 42)
scenarios.R13: binary by 3 groups, exact = TRUE -> Fisher's exact test
scenarios.R14: numeric 3 groups, var_equal FALSE and TRUE -> F-test (ANOVA) p 0.617788 both; oneway.test Welch p 0.692124
scenarios.R15: numeric 2 groups -> Welch (default) / Student's two-sample t-test (var_equal = TRUE)
scenarios.P1: paired binary exact -> Exact McNemar's test p 0.507813 = exact2x2::mcnemar.exact
scenarios.P2: paired binary asymptotic -> McNemar's test p 0.504985 = mcnemar.test(correct = TRUE) (correct = FALSE gives 0.317311); unpaired-CI warning
scenarios.P3: paired, one subject missing -> pair removed with warning
scenarios.P4: paired numeric with ID 31 twice in t0 and ID 32 twice in t1 -> Student's paired t-test p 0.827561, no warning; correctly matched IDs give 0.300278
scenarios.P5: 3 occasions binary complete -> Cochran's Q test
scenarios.P5b: same with one missing response -> 'Test errored' (tibble size mismatch)
scenarios.P6: paired numeric 3 occasions -> Mixed model ANOVA
scenarios.P7: paired nominal 3 categories (exact FALSE and TRUE) -> 'No test'
scenarios.P9: ordered factor, no group -> Wilcoxon's one-sample signed-rank test p 5.96e-08
scenarios.P10: numeric mean about 100, no group -> Student's one-sample t-test p 9.7e-14
scenarios.P11: numeric nonparametric 2 groups -> Mann-Whitney's U test with HL CI
scenarios.P12: Friedman with an incomplete block -> 'Test errored'
scenarios.P13: event level order reversed -> same Boschloo p, CI sign flipped
scenarios.M1: binary with 2 missing values, exact -> Boschloo (missing excluded)
scenarios.M3: include_group_missings_in_test = TRUE with missing groups -> Fisher's exact test
scenarios.O1: override Boschloo on 3-category variable -> p 0.0937317 = boschloo(5, 20, 1, 22) (first level vs rest)
scenarios.O2: override Boschloo with 3 groups -> p of groups A vs B only
scenarios.O3: boschloo_max_n = NULL at n = 42 -> Boschloo; boschloo_max_n = 10 -> Fisher with warning
scenarios.O5: global override Boschloo -> also applied to a numeric variable (p 0.748222)
